objective: Commit one hash-pinned Python 3.12 dependency lock for the root runtime, generated by a deterministic tool that resolves the ranges declared in pyproject.toml and records every wheel's sha256, make CI, Docker, bootstrap and the release manifest read that same lock, prove an offline install succeeds from a populated cache with --require-hashes, and fail visibly on drift or a yanked pin instead of silently re-resolving.
decision_supported: Can a reviewer confirm from the committed lock file and a re-runnable command alone that the root Python environment is resolved from exact, hash-checked artifacts, that an offline install from a populated cache reproduces it, that a re-resolution which would pick a different version is refused rather than silently accepted, and that the release provenance records the lock revision together with the resolved package hashes?
acceptance: a committed Python 3.12 lock artifact pins every distribution as name==version with at least one sha256 hash, and each pinned version satisfies the range declared in pyproject.toml
one tool generates the lock from the pyproject ranges and one offline subcommand verifies it without network access, with exit codes 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 INCOMPLETE

the lock is installed with --require-hashes, and because pip cannot hash an editable local project the editable install is a separate --no-deps step that the Makefile, the Dockerfile and CI all run in the same order
an offline install from a populated cache with PIP_NO_INDEX=1 and PIP_FIND_LINKS reproduces the pinned set and imports a pinned distribution without contacting an index
a re-resolution that would select a different version, or a pin that the index no longer offers, is reported as drift with a non-zero exit rather than silently accepted
the release manifest records the hashed lock revision together with the resolved package hashes, and refuses a lock whose hashes are absent or malformed
ROS, apt and the container-only MuJoCo capability environment stay outside the root Python lock scope, and the boundary is documented
the update policy names who resolves, who reviews, how a pin moves and how the lock is regenerated, and a weekly Dependabot update cannot move a pin without a human review
no production module, interface schema, contract model or firmware source is modified by this change

the two baseline tests that pinned the previous range-based install command are updated to assert the hash-checked install order instead, so they keep checking that CI builds the docs and that the image installs the project rather than a literal command string
evidence: Task Packet schema validation output with exit code
a drift run naming the version a re-resolution would change, and a run naming a pin the index no longer offers, both exiting 1
a drift run over a lock with one moved pin showing version_drift and exit code 1, and a drift run naming a package the index no longer offers showing withdrawn_pin and exit code 1
a re-resolution run over the committed lock showing it still reproduces with exit code 0
a verify run over the committed lock showing exit code 0, and a verify run over a mutated lock showing exit code 1 and the named defect
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed

mutation probes: neutering the missing-hash rule, the malformed-pin rule, the duplicate-pin rule, the per-package hash rule, the range check and the uncovered-requirement rule each makes a named test fail; the tool is restored byte-identically and confirmed with diff -q and sha256sum
ruff check, ruff format --check, the full pytest run, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check, make context-check and make docs output with exit codes
targeted pytest output for the dependency lock and the release provenance contracts
the committed lock file with its name==version --hash=sha256 pins and the count of pinned distributions
the offline install command and its output showing --require-hashes succeeded with PIP_NO_INDEX=1 from a populated PIP_FIND_LINKS directory
the updated baseline tests passing, and a mutation probe showing they still fail when the locked install order is replaced by the old range install
stop_conditions: Meeting the acceptance requires changing a dependency range in pyproject.toml or editing the MuJoCo capability lock.
Reproducible resolution requires a private index, a credential or a network call at verification time.
The lock can only be installed by weakening --require-hashes, for example by hashing an editable local project.
A pin cannot be verified offline without contacting an index.
data_classification: internal; the lock records public PyPI distribution names, versions and wheel hashes, and reads no credential, token or private index URL
model_policy: no model call; resolution, hashing and verification are deterministic and, apart from the explicit generate and re-resolve subcommands, offline
risks_and_fallbacks: pip cannot hash an editable local project, so a single --require-hashes install of .[dev] fails. The lock covers third-party distributions only and the editable project is installed as a separate --no-deps step in the same order everywhere.

A platform-specific lock is not portable across architectures. The lock records its target platform and Python version in its header and verify refuses a lock whose header disagrees with the running interpreter.

A stale lock silently pins a vulnerable version. The weekly Dependabot update still proposes range changes, the re-resolve subcommand reports what would move, and a human reviews the regenerated lock.
Committing a large lock makes review noisy. The lock is generated, sorted and grouped by a deterministic tool, so a diff shows exactly the pins that moved.

Editing CI and the Dockerfile changes how every job installs dependencies. The install order is the same three commands locally, in CI and in the container, and the Makefile target runs the identical sequence.

Updating the two baseline checks that pinned the previous range-based install command touches hardware/tools/validate_operations_readiness.py, which needs integration review because it is a build and CI configuration check. The edit replaces a literal command string with the invariant that check was always trying to assert, and hardware/tools is the only hardware path this task opens.
